Updated assessment with SLOOS lens:

- Policy stance: The “insurance” rate cut and early end to balance-sheet runoff remain appropriate given muted inflation and global uncertainties.
- SLOOS cross-check (July 2019):
  - Business credit: Banks tightened standards for C&I loans and for construction/land development loans; other lending terms tightened across firm sizes. Demand for construction/land development loans was weaker. These signals point to a softer credit supply-demand backdrop for businesses.
  - Consumer credit: Reports suggest willingness to lend in some other consumer loan categories with generally unchanged demand, but some tightening in standards for other consumer loans. Net effect on household credit is mixed-to-slightly tighter.
  - Government loans: Some stronger demand and unchanged standards in places, but not enough to offset business-sector tightening.
- Implications: SLOOS indicates emerging headwinds to business investment via tighter credit and weaker demand, reinforcing the FOMC’s caution about soft capex and supporting a modestly accommodative stance. Combined with FSR-noted vulnerabilities (elevated corporate leverage, thin risk compensation), risks are skewed slightly to the downside despite strong labor markets and firmer household spending.

Net tone: Still cautiously positive but more subdued once SLOOS tightening and weaker business loan demand are incorporated.
